text.headline: Timeline of Bulgaria
text.text: Major events in the history of Bulgaria.

events.headline: Foundation of the First Bulgarian Empire
events.text: The First Bulgarian Empire was established in 681 AD when Khan Asparuh united the Bulgarian tribes and settled in the region of modern-day Bulgaria.

events.headline: Christianization of Bulgaria
events.text: In 864, Tsar Boris I adopted Christianity as the state religion, marking a significant cultural shift and the beginning of the Christianization of the Bulgarian people.

events.headline: Recognition of Bulgarian Patriarchate
events.text: In 927, the Byzantine Empire recognized the Bulgarian Patriarchate, elevating Bulgaria's status in the Christian world and solidifying its independence.

events.headline: Byzantine Conquest of Bulgaria
events.text: In 1018, the Byzantine Empire conquered Bulgaria, leading to a period of Byzantine rule that lasted until the late 12th century.

events.headline: Establishment of the Second Bulgarian Empire
events.text: The Second Bulgarian Empire was established in 1185 after the successful rebellion of the brothers Asen and Peter against Byzantine rule, restoring Bulgarian sovereignty.

events.headline: Ottoman Conquest of Bulgaria
events.text: Bulgaria fell under Ottoman rule in 1396, marking the beginning of nearly five centuries of Ottoman domination over the region.

events.headline: Liberation from Ottoman Rule
events.text: The Russo-Turkish War (1877-1878) led to the liberation of Bulgaria from Ottoman rule, culminating in the Treaty of San Stefano.

events.headline: Bulgaria Declares Independence
events.text: On September 22, 1908, Bulgaria declared independence from the Ottoman Empire, establishing itself as a sovereign nation.

events.headline: First Balkan War
events.text: The First Balkan War began in 1912, where Bulgaria, along with its allies, fought against the Ottoman Empire to gain territory in the Balkans.

events.headline: Second Balkan War
events.text: The Second Balkan War erupted in 1913 as Bulgaria sought to expand its territory, leading to conflict with its former allies and resulting in territorial losses.

events.headline: Bulgaria Joins World War I
events.text: Bulgaria entered World War I on the side of the Central Powers in 1915, seeking to regain territories lost in the Balkan Wars.

events.headline: End of World War I
events.text: The end of World War I in 1918 resulted in Bulgaria's defeat and the signing of the Treaty of Neuilly, which imposed significant territorial losses and reparations.

events.headline: Soviet Occupation and Communist Rule
events.text: In 1944, the Soviet Army entered Bulgaria, leading to the establishment of a communist regime that lasted until 1989.

events.headline: Fall of Communism
events.text: The fall of communism in Bulgaria in 1989 marked the beginning of democratic reforms and the transition to a market economy.

events.headline: Bulgaria Joins NATO
events.text: Bulgaria became a member of NATO on March 29, 2004, enhancing its security and defense cooperation with Western nations.

events.headline: Bulgaria Joins the European Union
events.text: On January 1, 2007, Bulgaria officially joined the European Union, marking a significant step in its integration into European political and economic structures.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic reached Bulgaria in early 2020, leading to widespread health measures and impacting the economy and daily life.

events.headline: Political Turmoil and Elections
events.text: Bulgaria experienced significant political turmoil in 2021, leading to multiple elections and ongoing debates over governance and corruption.

events.headline: Ongoing Economic Challenges
events.text: Bulgaria continues to face economic challenges, including inflation and energy dependence, as it navigates post-pandemic recovery and geopolitical tensions.
